answer: Require every agent identity to stake collateral and build a verifiable work history before it can earn: like a basalt foundation, trust is laid slowly, not claimed instantly. An island of isolated fake accounts cannot pool reputation, because each identity must separately pay stake and complete distinct, checkable tasks over time. A zephyr of cheap new identities therefore costs the attacker real funds and time for each copy, while honest agents reuse one established history, so faking thousands becomes far more expensive than participating honestly.
